_OBJECTIVE: Verify that target RCS produces a measurable detection-count differential. A 20 dBsm airliner must produce at least 1.15x more detections per scan than a -10 dBsm stealth UAV at a range where the R^4 radar equation exposes the SNR gap.
_PASS_CRITERIA: Detection count for 20 dBsm target > 1.15x detection count for -10 dBsm target at 100 km range.
_GEOMETRY_NOTE: Uses tc05_PSR_longrange.json (111 km refRange / 111 km rangeLimits / refRCS=0) with rcs_demo targets at 100 km. The probabilistic RCS filter computes SNR_factor = (sigma/sigma_ref) * (refRange/R)^4 per detection and keeps it with probability Pd_scale = max(0.05, min(1, SNR_factor)). Airliner (20 dBsm, 100 m^2) at 100 km: SNR_factor ~152 -> Pd_scale=1.0 -> all kept. Stealth (-10 dBsm, 0.1 m^2) at 105 km: SNR_factor ~0.13 -> Pd_scale=0.13 -> ~13% kept. Expected ratio ~7-8x, well above the 1.15x threshold.
_IMPL_NOTE: v3.4.2: rcs_range_filter is enabled here because fusionRadarSensor's native Swerling detection model does not produce an observable RCS-vs-range differential at typical scan counts (20-30 scans) -- empirically both high-RCS and low-RCS targets saturate near DetectionProbability. The external filter applies a probabilistic R^4 Pd scaling on top of the sensor model, with a 5% floor for sidelobe leakage. For user demo scenarios (non-validation), rcs_range_filter remains OFF by default so they rely on the sensor-native model.
description: TC-05: RCS demo - Boeing 737 (20 dBsm) vs Stealth UAV (-10 dBsm) at 100 km, clear weather, probabilistic RCS filter ON
